name: Djibouti
snapshot: A tiny Red Sea port state that hosts American, Chinese, French and Japanese bases, where Ismaïl Omar Guelleh won a sixth term in 2026 with 97.8 percent.
culture: Djibouti's two main communities, the Somali Issa and the Afar, have distinct languages and traditions, and politics has long been balanced between them. Chewing khat, imported daily from Ethiopia, is an afternoon social ritual. Lake Assal, the lowest point in Africa, and the salt flats and volcanic landscapes of the Afar depression draw adventurous tourists.
society: The economy runs on its port, which handles most of landlocked Ethiopia's trade, and on rent from foreign bases at the mouth of the Red Sea. China built its first overseas military base here. Despite this income, unemployment is high and many people live in poverty. Houthi attacks on shipping since 2023 have hit traffic through the nearby Bab el-Mandeb strait.
situation: Djibouti is a country of about a million people that matters far more than its size suggests, because it sits on the Bab el-Mandeb, the narrow strait where the Red Sea meets the Gulf of Aden and much of Europe-Asia trade passes. The US, China, France and Japan all have military bases there, and the rent, along with Ethiopia's port traffic, keeps the economy running. That strategic value has also helped one family keep running the country.

On 10 April, President Ismaïl Omar Guelleh, 78, won a sixth term with 97.81 percent against a single challenger, a former ruling-party member (AP via WSLS). He had promised his fifth term would be his last; then, in October 2025, parliament unanimously scrapped the 75-year age limit that stood in his way. The two main opposition parties have boycotted every election since 2016, after he abolished term limits in 2010 (International IDEA). Guelleh succeeded his uncle, Djibouti's first president, in 1999. Foreign powers that depend on their bases there have said little.
power: A presidential republic in form, a dominant-party state in practice. The president is directly elected for five years with no term limit and appoints the prime minister and government; the ruling coalition dominates the National Assembly.
holders: President Ismaïl Omar Guelleh, in office since 1999.
